title: Prove sharp asymmetric coordinate-SWAP tariffs with dirty spectators
head: 9fb1552f12ca4777ca660461a8b602e709285f99
body:
PR #2444's asymmetric-label Open question 2 can be closed without weighted BFS. For any nonnegative fixed prices A,B, t coordinate SWAP targets, and any finite number of restored dirty spectator roles, the exact formal-model minimum is `t*(2*min(A,B)+max(A,B))`.

The new argument proves the individual bounds `#a>=t` and `#b>=t` by upper/lower crossing ranks in the natural representation, including arbitrary free scalar mixing. Combining them with Ross Richardson's credited #1989/#2415 total bound `#a+#b>=3t` proves the weighted lower bound. Independent per-role aba or bab words attain it. Zero tariffs are included; negative tariffs give an explicit unbounded identity-loop counterexample. This is a sharp tariff corollary, not a new uniform 3t theorem or native supplier.

Validation: optimized CPython3.12 registered replay passed; 54 full formal endpoints, 1,302 individual paid-factor charges, 144 free-mixing compositions, 2,160 mixed prefixes and 48,525 exact rational weighted inequalities. Controls cover the nonfaithful natural projection, each missing count inequality, omitted calls and changed labels/prices. Git-free unchanged replay, complete receipt rejection and exclusive regeneration passed. Separate AI proof review is recorded in TASK.json; no human or hosted CI pass is claimed.

Starts from refreshed canonical main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4. Original picker and explicit handoff scope change, exact predecessor pins, attribution and complete overlap freshness are recorded. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No frozen source or selected frontier change.
